summary: David Kopf was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1960–1964) and held a post at the University of Minnesota from around 1967 to 1997.
David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1972–1976) and held positions at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (~1993).

David L. McMahan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, and held posts as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

David L. Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Southampton, Queens' College, Cambridge, and under figures including Harold Walter Bailey and Walter Simon. He spent his career at the University of London and SOAS (~1950–1982).
David Ludden is a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia (~1979–1981), the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–2007), and New York University (~2007).

David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the School for International Training and the University of Virginia (PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer), later holding a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor (attested 1975, 1998–2001) and Professor of South Asian Studies and Chair of Religious Studies (attested 1989).
David Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Director of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004) and held a post there attested in 2013.
David N. Keightley was a sinologist and historian who served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1985 and 1999).

David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian. He studied at SOAS and the Australian National University (doctoral supervisor A. L. Basham), and he held a long-term post as professor and research scholar at El Colegio de México (~1970).

David Ownby is a scholar in sinology, religious studies, and history. After earning his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1982–1989), he held posts at Harvard (1991), Southern Methodist University (attested 1994), and Université de Montréal (from ~1993).

David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Washington (BA, MA, PhD under David Seyfort Ruegg), he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and University of Hamburg (~1988–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under the doctoral supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

David Phillip Stanley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and has held posts at Naropa University and the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Harvard University (1950–1960). He held posts at Harvard, Chicago, the American University of Beirut, the Institute for Advanced Study, and served as a professor at Brown University (1971).

David R. Loy is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, University of Hawaii, and National University of Singapore (PhD 1984), where he also taught (~1978–1984), later serving as professor at Xavier University (~2006–2008).

David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Colorado Boulder, Tokyo, and Stanford (PhD under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure), later becoming an associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, he held posts at Gonville and Caius, Jesus College, the University of Michigan (1968–1975), and Harvard University (1975–1982).
David Ruddell was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and held a post as Secretary at Fort William College.
